visuals.title: Where antiplatelets bleed
visuals.text: Minor bleeds at skin and mucosa; major bleeds in the gut and brain.

visuals.title: Managing a bleed
nodes: Treat source: endoscopy or IV fluids, transfusion

glossary.platelet aggregation: Platelets sticking to each other to form a plug at a site of vessel injury.
glossary.bruising: Bleeding under the skin from damaged small vessels, seen as a purple or blue mark.
glossary.gum bleeding: Bleeding from the gums, often on brushing; a common minor sign of impaired platelet function.
glossary.GI bleeding: Bleeding anywhere in the gut, from the oesophagus to the anus.
glossary.intracranial haemorrhage: Bleeding inside the skull, such as into the brain or its surrounding spaces.
glossary.hypotension: Low blood pressure, here a sign of significant blood loss.
glossary.pallor: Unusually pale skin, often a sign of anaemia or shock.
glossary.anaemic: Having a low haemoglobin, so blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.malaena: Black, tarry, foul-smelling stool from digested blood, usually an upper GI bleed (also spelt melaena).
glossary.MI: Myocardial infarction: death of heart muscle from blocked coronary blood flow.
glossary.stroke: Sudden loss of brain function from a blocked or burst blood vessel in the brain.
glossary.coronary stent: A small mesh tube placed in a coronary artery to keep it open after angioplasty.
glossary.cardiovascular disease: Disease of the heart and blood vessels, such as angina, MI, stroke and peripheral arterial disease.
glossary.irreversibly: Permanently; the drug cannot come off, so the effect lasts until new platelets are made.
glossary.acetylates: Adds an acetyl group to a protein; aspirin does this to COX-1, permanently switching it off.
glossary.renal effects: Effects on the kidneys, such as reduced blood flow and function from blocked prostaglandins.
glossary.esomeprazole: A proton pump inhibitor, closely related to omeprazole, that also inhibits CYP2C19.
glossary.ticlopidine: An older thienopyridine antiplatelet drug, now rarely used, also linked to TTP.
glossary.microvascular platelet thrombi: Small platelet clots blocking tiny blood vessels throughout the body, as in TTP.
glossary.gastroprotective prostaglandins: Prostaglandins that protect the stomach lining by increasing mucus, bicarbonate and blood flow.
glossary.prostaglandins: Lipid signalling molecules made by COX enzymes, with roles in inflammation, pain and stomach protection.
glossary.peptic ulceration: Formation of ulcers in the stomach or duodenum where acid erodes the lining.
glossary.occult blood loss: Hidden bleeding that is not visible but shows up as anaemia or on testing.
glossary.overt blood loss: Visible bleeding, such as haematemesis or melaena.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red cells; falls with blood loss.
glossary.coagulation profile: Blood tests of the clotting cascade, usually PT, INR and APTT.
glossary.anticoagulant: A drug that blocks the clotting cascade, such as warfarin or a DOAC.
glossary.resuscitation: Restoring circulation and blood volume, here with IV fluids and blood transfusion.
glossary.transfusion: Giving donated blood or blood products into a vein.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given into a vein to restore circulating volume.
glossary.thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a vessel, such as a stent or coronary artery.
glossary.perioperative: Around the time of surgery, including before, during and after.
glossary.reversal: Undoing a drug's effect on clotting, for warfarin by giving vitamin K.
glossary.haemostasis: The body's process of stopping bleeding: platelet plug then fibrin clot.
glossary.von Willebrand factor: A large blood protein that sticks platelets to damaged vessel walls; cut to size by ADAMTS13.
glossary.NICE CKS: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries: practical UK guidance for primary care.
